paragraphs.heading: What a Mars rover is
paragraphs.text: A Mars rover is a motor vehicle, driven by remote control, that travels across the surface of Mars. Rovers have clear advantages over landers that stay in one place. They can cover more ground, be sent toward interesting features, and move into sunny spots to get through the winter months. They also do a different job from spacecraft that orbit Mars, such as Mars Reconnaissance Orbiter.

paragraphs.heading: Six that worked
paragraphs.text: As of May 2021, six robotic rovers had worked successfully on Mars. NASA's Jet Propulsion Laboratory ran the first five. Sojourner landed in 1997, Spirit and Opportunity in 2004, Curiosity in 2012 and Perseverance in 2021. The sixth was Zhurong, run by the China National Space Administration. When it began operating on May 14, 2021, it became the first rover from outside the United States to work on Mars.

paragraphs.heading: Sojourner and Spirit
paragraphs.text: Sojourner, part of Mars Pathfinder, landed on July 4, 1997. It drove a little over 100 meters before contact was lost on September 27 that year. Spirit landed on January 4, 2004. By nearly six years after its original mission limit it had covered 7.73 km, but then its wheels got stuck in sand. Its last signal came on March 22, 2010.

paragraphs.heading: Opportunity's record
paragraphs.text: Opportunity landed on January 25, 2004. It beat the earlier records for how long a rover lasted, working for 5,352 sols, or 5,498 Earth days from landing to the end of its mission, and it drove 45.16 km. In June 2018 a global dust storm on Mars blocked the sunlight it needed to recharge its batteries, and it sent its last status on 10 June. After hundreds of tries to wake it, NASA declared the mission complete on February 13, 2019.

paragraphs.heading: Curiosity and Perseverance
paragraphs.text: Curiosity launched on November 26, 2011 and landed in Gale Crater on August 6, 2012, near the mountain informally called Mount Sharp. It is still working as of November 2026. Perseverance is built on Curiosity's successful design. It landed on February 18, 2021, carrying the Mars helicopter Ingenuity attached to its belly. Ingenuity's mission has ended, but Perseverance is still working as of November 2026.

paragraphs.heading: Zhurong
paragraphs.text: Zhurong landed on May 14, 2021, in the southern part of Utopia Planitia. It was designed to last 90 sols, yet stayed active for 347 sols and drove 1,921 m. In May 2022 it was switched off ahead of sandstorms and the Martian winter. More dust than expected then piled onto its solar panels, so it could not switch itself back on.

paragraphs.heading: Looking for signs of life
paragraphs.text: NASA has made the search for evidence of habitability, of fossils and of organic carbon on Mars a primary goal. In 2016 the agency said Opportunity and Curiosity would look for traces of ancient life. They would also look for signs of ancient water, including old river and lake settings that may once have been habitable.
